name: Nourished by Time
label: XL Recordings
lede: A Baltimore kid who stocked shelves at Whole Foods, cut a zero-dollar album in his parents' basement, and ended up on Pitchfork's year-end top ten.

eras.title: Riley With Fire, then a mantra
eras.text: Marcus Brown wrote under two other names before settling on one he says is a reminder to keep going. He was working retail in Baltimore when the songs started stacking up.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nourished by Time · Tone Glow 133 · The Face
years.h: Brown drops two aliases and becomes Nourished by Time
years.p: After Riley With Fire and Mother Marcus, he settles on a name he calls "a mantra about staying consistent", a nod to Guided by Voices.
years.xp:
Brown enrolled at Berklee College of Music in Boston at 17, where he credits the songwriting teacher Pat Pattison as "the only professor who let me be weird". Riley With Fire was the first project he ever wrote songs for, a college-sophomore thing steered by Foxygen, Mac DeMarco and Youth Lagoon, per Tone Glow.

He told The Face the name works as a reminder, and that he never wanted to release music under his own. Wikipedia notes the wording also echoes Guided by Voices.

years.src: Tone Glow 133 · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Los Angeles runs out of money, so Brown goes home to Baltimore
years.p: He'd moved to LA after college, inspired by David Lynch films, and worked there for two years before returning just before COVID.
years.xp:
The Los Angeles years included night shifts stocking shelves at Whole Foods in Koreatown, then a hunt for parking afterward, with little time for sleep or dating before the music got its turn. Per Tone Glow he came back to Baltimore because of money.

Back in his parents' house, he had a basement, a guitar and a lot of lockdown.

eras.title: A zero-dollar album in the basement
eras.text: Erotic Probiotic 2 came out on a small label and was written up as the year's best pop record by more than one critic. Brown was touring with Dry Cleaning within months.

years.h: Touring the US with [[Dry Cleaning|8a74e5ea-6f68-49e1-951c-80d2291f7c3f]] before the album is even out
years.p: Brown opened US dates for the London post-punk band in January 2023, and later remixed their single Gary Ashby.

years.src: Wikipedia: Erotic Probiotic 2 · Wikipedia: Nourished by Time
years.h: Erotic Probiotic 2: 34 minutes, no budget, one basement
years.p: Brown recorded and mixed it himself in his parents' Baltimore house, with a Roland Juno-106 he bought after a Dogecoin bet paid off.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the album was made with a zero-dollar budget while Brown had COVID-19, which he says hurt the mixing and vocals. He calls it "just a ball of emotion", written around a breakup while he was working at Whole Foods. The sound stacks R&B, freestyle, shoegaze, post-punk and Baltimore club.

Asked about class and pop stardom, he said: "Name one socialist pop star, it doesn't exist."

years.h: Pitchfork gives Erotic Probiotic 2 an 8.2 and Best New Music
years.p: It later placed the album No. 5 on its 2023 year-end list; Gorilla vs. Bear named it album of the year.

years.h: On Yaeji's debut, plus a remix for [[Water from Your Eyes|09f91305-e193-48af-92e3-252b3dd5e718]]
years.p: Brown appears on "Happy" from [[Yaeji|2d781050-032a-4a4f-b0a9-7b4bc99449e1]]'s With a Hammer and reworks Water from Your Eyes' "True Life".

eras.title: XL comes calling
eras.text: A major indie label took the basement record and the songs that followed it. Brown answered with a short, sharp EP and one of his best-loved songs.

years.h: Nourished by Time signs to XL Recordings
years.p: Wikipedia dates the deal to February 2024, a year after Scenic Route put out Brown's debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nourished by Time · Paste: Nourished By Time Is Possessed
years.h: Catching Chickens EP, his first for XL
years.p: It arrived digitally on March 22 and on vinyl in May, with "Hand on Me" and "Hell of a Ride" as its calling cards.
years.xp: Paste ranked "Hell of a Ride" No. 6 on its list of the best songs of 2024. Pitchfork reviewed the EP the week it came out.

eras.title: Post-R&B, top ten
eras.text: Brown's second album came out in a rush of singles, tour dates and critical love. Pitchfork put it among the best of the year.

years.h: XL reissues Erotic Probiotic 2 on vinyl
years.p: The reissue brought the basement album to a wider release two years after it first appeared.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Passionate Ones · Wikipedia: Nourished by Time
years.p: The lead single samples Labi Siffre's "Saved"; Brown directed the video himself.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Passionate Ones · Wikipedia: Nourished by Time
years.p: Second single from The Passionate Ones, with a video directed by Cody Marian.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Passionate Ones · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2025 · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: The Passionate Ones: Pitchfork 8.4, Best New Music, No. 9 of 2025
years.p: Twelve songs, 44:58, recorded across Baltimore, London and New York; Brown wrote, played, produced, mixed and engineered it himself.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 8.4 and Best New Music, then ranked it No. 9 on its list of the 50 best albums of 2025, between Joanne Robertson's Blurrr and Amaarae's Black Star. Metacritic lists 89 out of 100 from 15 reviews; The Line of Best Fit gave it 9/10 and Paste named it album of the year.

Tony Bontana guests on "Jojo". "Crazy People" uses a sample from a Library of Congress collection of letters to a president, per Wikipedia.

years.p: Brown told The Line of Best Fit he'd rather challenge listeners than make them happy, and that nostalgia isn't the point.
years.xp: In the same interview he says: "Everyone is inspired by nostalgia, but I'm not reliving anything." On what success has changed: "Money hasn't changed anything. I'm just more confused about how to help."

years.src: Wikipedia: Nourished by Time · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: 25 dates across North America and Europe
years.p: Brown moved to New York in August and took the record on the road for a three-month run, per Wikipedia and Bandcamp Daily.
